lesson.summary: Secure workloads by layering controls: segment networks with subnets, security groups, and network ACLs; keep traffic private with NAT and VPC endpoints; filter web traffic with AWS WAF and Shield; detect threats with GuardDuty and Inspector; and manage credentials with Secrets Manager and IAM roles.
keyPoints: Security groups are stateful and allow rules only; network ACLs are stateless with allow and deny rules
Reference security groups as sources to restrict tiers
NAT gateway gives private subnets outbound-only internet access
Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB are free and keep traffic private
WAF filters layer 7 requests; Shield protects against DDoS
Secrets Manager rotates database credentials automatically
GuardDuty detects threats, Inspector finds vulnerabilities, Firewall Manager applies policies centrally

scenarios.text: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets behind an Application Load Balancer. The application connects to an Amazon RDS database using a password that is hardcoded in the code. Compliance now requires the password to rotate every 30 days, and no long-lived AWS access keys may be stored on the instances.

A retail company is launching a customer portal. The front end calls a REST API built with Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Customers must register and sign in with email and password, only signed-in users may call the API, and the company wants protection against common web exploits such as SQL injection. The team is small and wants to avoid managing servers.

questions.prompt: A three-tier application has public web servers, private application servers, and a private database. The database must accept connections only from the application servers, even if their IP addresses change. What is the best way to configure this?

options.text: Allow the application subnet CIDR range in the database network ACL only
Allow 0.0.0.0/0 on the database port and rely on the database password
Reference the application tier security group as the source in the database security group inbound rule
Place the database in the public subnet with an elastic IP address

questions.explanation: Security groups can use another security group as a source, so only members of the application tier can connect regardless of their IPs. A subnet-wide network ACL rule is broader and stateless. Opening to the internet relies on only one control. A public subnet with an elastic IP exposes the database unnecessarily.

questions.prompt: EC2 instances in a private subnet must download operating system patches from the internet, and the internet must not be able to initiate connections to them. Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Attach an internet gateway and give each instance a public IP address
Create a VPC peering connection to the default VPC
Add a Site-to-Site VPN connection
Deploy a NAT gateway in a public subnet and route the private subnet's default route to it

questions.explanation: A NAT gateway allows outbound internet access from private instances while blocking unsolicited inbound connections. Public IPs on instances make them reachable from the internet. Peering and VPN do not provide internet egress for patches.

questions.prompt: A public web application behind an Application Load Balancer is being probed with SQL injection and cross-site scripting requests. Which service blocks these requests with the least operational effort?

options.text: AWS WAF with managed rule groups associated to the ALB
AWS Shield Standard
Amazon GuardDuty
A network ACL that denies the attacker IP addresses

questions.explanation: AWS WAF inspects HTTP requests at layer 7 and managed rule groups cover common injection and XSS patterns. Shield Standard protects against network and transport layer DDoS, not application payloads. GuardDuty detects threats but does not block requests. Network ACLs cannot inspect request content and attacker IPs change.

questions.prompt: A Lambda function runs in private subnets with no internet route and must write to Amazon S3. The company wants the lowest cost and traffic that stays on the AWS network. What should the architect add?

options.text: A NAT gateway in each Availability Zone
An S3 interface endpoint with a per-hour charge
A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 and a route table entry for it
An internet gateway with a public IP on the function

questions.explanation: A gateway endpoint for S3 adds a route to the private subnets, keeps traffic on the AWS network, and has no additional charge. A NAT gateway adds hourly and per-GB charges. An interface endpoint works but adds hourly cost. Lambda functions in a VPC do not get public IPs, and an internet gateway would not fix that.

questions.prompt: Which TWO actions help protect an internet-facing web application from DDoS attacks? (Choose two.)

options.text: Place CloudFront in front of the application and enable AWS Shield Advanced on it
Add an AWS WAF rate-based rule to limit requests per IP address
Open all ports in the security group so legitimate traffic is not blocked
Disable logging to reduce load
Move the application to a single larger instance

questions.explanation: CloudFront absorbs traffic at edge locations and Shield Advanced adds enhanced DDoS protection and response support, while a WAF rate-based rule throttles abusive sources. Opening all ports increases exposure. Disabling logging removes visibility. One larger instance remains a single point that can be overwhelmed.

questions.statement: Security groups are stateful, so return traffic for an allowed inbound request is automatically allowed, whereas network ACLs are stateless.
questions.explanation: True. Security groups track connections, while network ACLs evaluate inbound and outbound rules separately and need both directions allowed.

questions.prompt: Match each AWS security service to what it does.

pairs.right: Detects threats by analyzing CloudTrail, VPC flow, and DNS logs
Scans EC2, ECR images, and Lambda for software vulnerabilities
Managed stateful and stateless traffic filtering for a VPC
Centrally applies WAF and security group policies across accounts

questions.explanation: Each pairing matches the service description in the AWS documentation.

questions.prompt: Where should the application store the database credentials to meet the 30-day rotation requirement with the least operational overhead?

options.text: In an encrypted file in the application's S3 bucket
In the EC2 user data script
In environment variables baked into the AMI
In AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation enabled

questions.explanation: Secrets Manager stores credentials and can rotate supported database secrets on a schedule using managed Lambda functions. Files in S3, user data, and AMI variables all require custom rotation and spread plaintext copies.

questions.prompt: How should the EC2 instances be authorized to retrieve the secret without storing any access keys?

options.text: Attach an instance profile role that allows secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on that secret only
Create an IAM user and store its keys in the Auto Scaling launch template
Make the secret readable by everyone through a resource policy
Copy the secret value into each instance at launch by hand

questions.explanation: An instance profile role supplies temporary credentials and can be scoped to one secret for least privilege. IAM user keys in the template are long-lived credentials. A public resource policy exposes the secret. Manual copying is error prone and defeats rotation.

questions.prompt: A company wants to inspect all outbound traffic from many VPCs and allow only specific domain names, with intrusion prevention rules and centrally managed policy. Which service fits best?

options.text: Security groups on every instance
AWS Network Firewall
Amazon Inspector
Network ACLs with allow rules for each IP

questions.explanation: AWS Network Firewall provides stateful inspection with domain-list filtering and intrusion prevention, and it can be managed centrally. Security groups cannot filter by domain name. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, not traffic. Network ACLs match IPs and ports only and cannot follow changing domain IPs.

questions.prompt: A startup builds a mobile app backed by Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Customers must sign up and sign in with email or a social identity provider, and the API must reject calls without a valid token. Which solution has the least operational overhead?

options.text: Store usernames and password hashes in a DynamoDB table and validate them in a Lambda authorizer
Create an IAM user for each customer and have the app sign requests with their access keys
Use an Amazon Cognito user pool with social federation and a Cognito authorizer on the API
Run an open-source identity server on EC2 and validate tokens in the application

questions.explanation: A Cognito user pool handles sign-up, sign-in, social federation and token issuance, and API Gateway can validate its tokens natively. Building your own credential store adds security and maintenance burden. IAM users for customers do not scale and require distributing long-lived keys. A self-run identity server on EC2 must be patched, scaled and secured by the team.

questions.prompt: A static website is served through Amazon CloudFront from a private S3 bucket. Users must only be able to read objects through CloudFront, not by calling the S3 URL directly. What should the architect configure?

options.text: Create a CloudFront origin access control and add a bucket policy that allows only the CloudFront distribution
Make the bucket public and rely on obscure object names
Add a security group to the bucket that allows only CloudFront IP ranges
Enable S3 versioning so direct reads return an older copy

questions.explanation: Origin access control lets CloudFront sign requests to S3, and the bucket policy then trusts only that distribution. A public bucket exposes every object to direct access. S3 buckets do not use security groups. Versioning does not restrict who can read objects.

questions.prompt: Which AWS service continuously analyzes CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs to detect suspicious activity such as an EC2 instance communicating with a known malicious IP address?

options.text: Amazon Inspector
AWS Config
AWS Artifact
Amazon GuardDuty

questions.explanation: GuardDuty is the managed threat detection service that analyzes these log sources for malicious behavior. Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities rather than detecting live threats. Config records resource configuration changes and compliance. Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements.

questions.prompt: A company stores millions of files in Amazon S3 and must find which buckets contain personally identifiable information, with minimal custom code. Which service should it use?

options.text: Amazon GuardDuty with S3 protection
Amazon Macie
AWS Shield Advanced
Amazon Detective

questions.explanation: Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover sensitive data such as PII in S3. GuardDuty detects suspicious access and threats, not data content classification. Shield Advanced protects against DDoS. Detective helps investigate findings but does not classify data.

questions.prompt: Containers running on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate need to read items from a DynamoDB table. Each service should have only the permissions it needs. What is the recommended way to grant access?

options.text: Put an IAM user access key in the container environment variables
Assign a task IAM role to each ECS task definition with a least-privilege policy
Attach a single administrator role to the cluster so every task can reach DynamoDB
Embed the access key in the container image

questions.explanation: A task role gives the containers temporary credentials scoped to that task. Access keys in environment variables or the image are long-lived and can leak. A shared administrator role breaks least privilege.

questions.prompt: A company encrypts S3 objects with a customer managed AWS KMS key. A new analytics account must be able to read the objects. The bucket policy already allows the account. Reads still fail with an access denied error from KMS. What is missing?

options.text: The KMS key policy or a grant must allow the analytics account principals to use kms:Decrypt
The bucket must be moved to the same Region as the analytics account
S3 Transfer Acceleration must be enabled on the bucket
The objects must be copied to a bucket that uses SSE-S3

questions.explanation: KMS access is governed by the key policy, so cross-account principals need permission there in addition to the S3 permission. Region alignment is not the cause of an authorization error. Transfer Acceleration affects upload speed only. Copying to SSE-S3 would work but changes the security design and is not what is missing.

questions.prompt: A company runs a web application behind an Application Load Balancer. Only customers in two specific countries are allowed to use it, and all other traffic must be blocked before reaching the application. Which approach is simplest?

options.text: Edit the security group to list the IP ranges of those countries
Use a network ACL that denies every other country by name
Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with a geographic match rule that allows only those countries
Enable AWS Config rules to flag requests from other countries

questions.explanation: AWS WAF can match on the request country of origin and be attached to an Application Load Balancer. Maintaining country IP lists in a security group is impractical and security groups cannot deny. Network ACLs match addresses, not country names. Config evaluates resource configuration and does not block requests.

questions.prompt: Which TWO actions help prevent accidental public exposure of data in Amazon S3 across an account? (Choose two.)

options.text: Give every developer s3:* permission so they can fix issues quickly
Turn on S3 Block Public Access at the account level
Use long, random bucket names
Use AWS Config or IAM Access Analyzer to detect buckets that allow public access
Disable default encryption

questions.explanation: Account-level Block Public Access overrides public ACLs and policies, and Access Analyzer or Config detects buckets that are shared publicly. Broad s3:* permissions increase the chance of mistakes. Random bucket names are not an access control. Disabling encryption does nothing for public exposure and weakens protection.

questions.prompt: A company must encrypt data at rest on its EC2 workloads with keys it controls and can audit. Which TWO choices meet this? (Choose two.)

options.text: Enable Amazon EBS encryption using a customer managed KMS key
Rely on security groups to protect the volume contents
Review AWS CloudTrail logs for KMS key usage
Store the plaintext key in an instance user data script
Use a network ACL to encrypt traffic to the volume

questions.explanation: EBS encryption with a customer managed key gives control over the key policy, and CloudTrail records each KMS API call for audit. Security groups and network ACLs filter network traffic and do not encrypt stored data. Keys in user data are exposed to anyone who can read it.

questions.prompt: Which design meets the requirements with the least operational overhead?

options.text: Run a custom login service on EC2, issue its own tokens, and have each Lambda function validate them in code
Give each customer an IAM user and require SigV4-signed API calls
Make the API public and filter requests by customer IP address
Use an Amazon Cognito user pool as the identity provider, protect the API Gateway methods with a Cognito authorizer, and enable AWS WAF on the API stage

questions.explanation: Cognito manages users and tokens, the API Gateway authorizer rejects unauthenticated calls, and WAF adds protection against common web exploits, all without servers to run. A custom login service on EC2 requires patching, scaling and token security work. IAM users for customers do not scale. Customer IP addresses change and do not identify users.

questions.prompt: Put these steps in a sensible order to let an EC2 application read a secret without storing access keys.
steps: Application uses the SDK to call GetSecretValue with the instance credentials
Create the secret in AWS Secrets Manager
Attach the instance profile to the EC2 instance
Create an IAM role with permission to read that secret
questions.explanation: The secret must exist first, then a role is granted permission to read it, then the role is attached to the instance through an instance profile, and finally the application can call Secrets Manager using temporary credentials delivered by the instance metadata service.
